"""The Monday command.

    uv run coachreport run
    uv run coachreport run --week N --season YYYY
    uv run coachreport run --offline
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys

from . import audit, config, payload, pdf, render, snapshot
from .resolve import NoCompletedGame, ResolvedWeek, current_season, resolve_week
from .sources import cfbd, pff


def _out_dir(season: int, week: int):
    return config.OUT / str(season) / f"wk{week:02d}"


def _load_or_pull(season, week, offline):
    """Return (snapshot, ResolvedWeek). One path builds, one path reloads.

    The offline path cannot know the next game — the cached snapshot was frozen
    at build time and carries no schedule beyond what the original pull saw fit
    to keep. `next_opponent` is passed through as None so `build_meta` degrades
    to "No further games" honestly, rather than printing "Week None". An offline
    rebuild is for checking a render, not for handing to a coach.
    """
    if offline:
        cached = sorted(config.OUT.glob(f"{season}/wk*/snapshot.json"))
        if not cached:
            raise NoCompletedGame(f"no cached snapshot for {season}")
        snap = json.loads(cached[-1].read_text())
        m = snap["meta"]
        rw = ResolvedWeek(m["year"], m["week"], m["game_id"], m["opponent"],
                          snap["game"]["home"] == config.TEAM,
                          None, None, None)
        return snap, rw

    client = cfbd.Client()
    games = client.get("/games", year=season, team=config.TEAM)
    rw = resolve_week(games, config.TEAM, season, week=week)
    con = pff.connect()
    try:
        return snapshot.build_snapshot(client, con, rw), rw
    finally:
        con.close()


def run(season=None, week=None, offline=False, force=False) -> int:
    season = season or current_season()
    try:
        snap, rw = _load_or_pull(season, week, offline)
    except NoCompletedGame as e:
        print(e, file=sys.stderr)
        return 3

    out = _out_dir(rw.season, rw.week)
    # SPEC §5: an explicit --week is documented as "override, for a rebuild" —
    # naming a week is already an intentional rebuild request. An --offline run
    # is a rebuild of what is already on disk by definition — the snapshot it
    # just loaded lives in this same directory. Only the default, un-overridden
    # online path (no --week, no --offline) needs the already-built guard.
    if out.exists() and not force and not offline and week is None:
        print(f"{out} already exists — week {rw.week} is already built. "
              f"Re-run with --force to rebuild.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 4

    out.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (out / "snapshot.json").write_text(json.dumps(snap, default=str))

    A, B = payload.build_payloads(snap, rw)
    failures = []
    for edition, data, name in (("coaches", A, "payload_a.json"),
                                ("performance", B, "payload_b.json")):
        (out / name).write_text(json.dumps(data, separators=(",", ":"), default=str))
        tiers = audit.no_tier_language(data)
        if tiers:
            failures.append(f"G10 {edition}: tier language {tiers}")
        html = render.render_edition(edition, data, out)
        pdf_path = pdf.to_pdf(html, out / f"{edition}.pdf")
        failures += [f"{edition}: {f}" for f in pdf.check_gates(html, pdf_path)]

    # SPEC G6 covers templates AND source. audit.py exempts config.py and itself.
    failures += audit.no_hardcoded_weekly_values(
        sorted(config.TEMPLATES.glob("*.html"))
        + sorted((config.REPO / "src/coachreport").rglob("*.py")))

    print(f"\n{config.TEAM} {rw.season} week {rw.week} "
          f"{'vs' if rw.home else 'at'} {rw.opponent}")
    print(f"next: {rw.next_opponent or 'none'}")
    print(f"wrote {out}")
    if failures:
        print("\nFAILED GATES:", file=sys.stderr)
        for f in failures:
            print(f"  - {f}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print("all gates passed")
    return 0


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="coachreport")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    r = sub.add_parser("run", help="build this week's two editions")
    r.add_argument("--season", type=int, default=None)
    r.add_argument("--week", type=int, default=None)
    r.add_argument("--offline", action="store_true",
                   help="rebuild from the cached snapshot, no API calls")
    r.add_argument("--force", action="store_true", help="rebuild a week already built")
    a = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if a.cmd == "run":
        return run(a.season, a.week, a.offline, a.force)
    return 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

The offline path (`_load_or_pull(..., offline=True)`) never constructs a
`cfbd.Client`, so every test here that uses `offline=True` makes zero network
calls — verified by never importing `requests` mocks at all: there is nothing

import json

from coachreport import cli, config, pdf


@pytest.fixture
def seeded_out(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

def test_offline_with_no_cached_snapshot_exits_3(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "OUT", tmp_path / "empty_out")

def test_already_built_online_path_exits_4_without_force(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    # Exercises the already-built guard on the (mocked) online path — no real
    # CFBD call: _load_or_pull is replaced outright, so cli.run never reaches
    # cfbd.Client().
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "OUT", tmp_path / "out")
    out = tmp_path / "out" / "2025" / "wk06"
    out.mkdir(parents=True)

    from coachreport.resolve import ResolvedWeek
    rw = ResolvedWeek(2025, 6, 401756911, "Kansas State", True, "TCU", 8, False)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "_load_or_pull", lambda season, week, offline: ({}, rw))

    assert cli.run(season=2025) == 4


def test_explicit_week_bypasses_the_already_built_guard(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    # SPEC §5 documents `--week` as "override, for a rebuild" — naming a week is
    # itself the intentional-rebuild signal, same as --force. This test is about
    # the guard only, so render/pdf are stubbed out rather than invoking real
    # Chrome — a Chrome-independent test should not need Chrome installed.
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "OUT", tmp_path / "out")
    out = tmp_path / "out" / "2025" / "wk06"
    out.mkdir(parents=True)

    from coachreport.resolve import ResolvedWeek
    rw = ResolvedWeek(2025, 6, 401756911, "Kansas State", True, "TCU", 8, False)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli, "_load_or_pull", lambda season, week, offline: ({}, rw))
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        "coachreport.payload.build_payloads",
        lambda snap, rw: ({"meta": {"note": "fine"}}, {"meta": {"note": "fine"}}))
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli.render, "render_edition",
                        lambda edition, data, out_dir: out_dir / f"{edition}.html")
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli.pdf, "to_pdf", lambda html, pdf_path: pdf_path)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli.pdf, "check_gates", lambda html, pdf_path: [])
    for name in ("coaches.html", "performance.html", "coaches.pdf", "performance.pdf"):
        (out / name).write_text("x")

    # exit, proving the guard — not the whole pipeline, which is stubbed — is
    # what bypassed.
    assert cli.run(season=2025, week=6) == 0

def test_offline_run_end_to_end_all_gates_pass(seeded_out):

def seeded_finale_out(tmp_path, monkeypatch):

    snap["ppa_next_opp"] = snap["adv_season_next_opp"] = []

def test_offline_run_degrades_next_game_honestly_not_with_the_literal_none(

    # back None and build_meta must say "No further games" -- never print the

Task 12 review is back: **Approved**, with two Important findings to close. The reviewer credited a lot specifically — `_load_or_pull` is a genuinely single load path with no draft residue and improves on the brief by closing the PFF connection in a `finally`; your `tokenize`+`ast` docstring/comment strip is narrow and well-proven; parser failure paths fail toward stricter rather than silently hiding hits; `tests/test_cli.py` earns its place as the only durable coverage of the exit-code branching; and commit `c9745ca` was a real bug you caught by measuring rather than assuming. I verified two of your three concerns myself. Here is what I found and what I'm ruling.

## Open finding 1 (Important) — `weak` prefix-matches `weakside`

Confirmed. I ran it:

```
FLAGS ['weak']  | weakside linebacker beat the block
FLAGS ['weak']  | strongside and weakside splits
FLAGS ['weak']  | a weak effort from the front seven
FLAGS clean     | above his own range for weeks 1 to 5
```

`audit.py` is wholly a Task 12 file, so "pre-existing brief design" does not put this out of reach. G10 exists to keep the copy descriptive, and a gate that fires on "weakside linebacker" is exactly the kind of false alarm that gets a gate switched off — which would then miss the real thing.

**Fix:** add a trailing word boundary — `re.search(rf"\b{w}\b", text)`. Not a negative lookahead; unnecessarily fragile for a fixed short list. Note this also stops matching stems like "weakness", which is correct: the list's intent is standalone tier adjectives ("an elite week", "a weak effort").

Add a test pinning both sides:

```python
def test_football_vocabulary_is_not_mistaken_for_a_verdict():
    # G10 must not fire on ordinary football terms, or it gets switched off.
    assert audit.no_tier_language({"note": "weakside linebacker beat the block"}) == []
    assert audit.no_tier_language({"note": "strongside and weakside splits"}) == []
    assert audit.no_tier_language({"note": "a weak effort from the front seven"}) == ["weak"]
```

## Open finding 2 (Important) — `--offline` silently ignores `--week`

Confirmed: the offline branch takes `week` and never reads it, always loading `sorted(cached)[-1]`. It is not data-corrupting, but silently discarding an explicit user argument is worse than refusing it — someone asks for week 4 offline, gets week 6, and the only clue is a line of output they may not read.

**Fix:** refuse the combination rather than guessing. In `_load_or_pull`'s offline branch, after loading the snapshot, if `week` was given and does not match the loaded snapshot's week, raise a clear error naming both:

```python
        if week is not None and week != snap["meta"]["week"]:
            raise NoCompletedGame(
                f"--offline reloads the most recent cached snapshot, which is week "
                f"{snap['meta']['week']}, not the week {week} you asked for. "
                f"Drop --offline to rebuild week {week} from the API.")
```

That routes through the existing exit-3 path. Add a test for it.

## Ruling — do NOT narrow the URL strip (reviewer's Minor 1)

The reviewer suggested scoping the URL strip to comments and docstrings, because a year hardcoded inside a URL in live code would be silently stripped. I checked, and narrowing would break a real case: `templates/*.tpl.html` contains `const NS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";` in **live JavaScript**, not a comment. Scoping the strip to comments would make that SVG namespace trip the year regex on every run.

So keep the strip as it is, and **document the limitation where the next reader will hit it**. Add a comment above `URL` in `audit.py` saying: the strip is deliberately blanket-wide because the SVG namespace URL appears in live template JavaScript and contains `2000`; the known cost is that a genuine year hardcoded inside a URL in live source would be missed.

`SPEC.md`'s G6 row says the audit excludes `config.py` but does not mention that `audit.py` self-exempts too (it holds the opponent list). Add `audit.py` to that sentence. Change nothing else.

"""The Monday command.

    uv run coachreport run
    uv run coachreport run --week N --season YYYY
    uv run coachreport run --offline
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys

from . import audit, config, payload, pdf, render, snapshot
from .resolve import NoCompletedGame, ResolvedWeek, current_season, resolve_week
from .sources import cfbd, pff


def _out_dir(season: int, week: int):
    return config.OUT / str(season) / f"wk{week:02d}"


def _load_or_pull(season, week, offline):
    """Return (snapshot, ResolvedWeek). One path builds, one path reloads.

    The offline path reconstructs the next game from `snapshot["schedule"]`,
    which is the whole season's week/opponent/home, not just the played games —
    it was measured to carry this, contrary to an earlier draft's assumption
    that next_week/next_home are simply unavailable offline. Only a genuine
    last-game-of-season snapshot (no schedule row past the frozen week) falls
    back to `next_opponent=None`, and `build_meta` degrades that to "No further
    games" honestly rather than printing the literal "Week None".
    """
    if offline:
        cached = sorted(config.OUT.glob(f"{season}/wk*/snapshot.json"))
        if not cached:
            raise NoCompletedGame(f"no cached snapshot for {season}")
        snap = json.loads(cached[-1].read_text())
        m = snap["meta"]
        later = sorted((g for g in snap.get("schedule", []) if g["week"] > m["week"]),
                       key=lambda g: g["week"])
        nxt = later[0] if later else None
        rw = ResolvedWeek(m["year"], m["week"], m["game_id"], m["opponent"],
                          snap["game"]["home"] == config.TEAM,
                          nxt["opponent"] if nxt else None,
                          nxt["week"] if nxt else None,
                          nxt["home"] if nxt else None)
        return snap, rw

    client = cfbd.Client()
    games = client.get("/games", year=season, team=config.TEAM)
    rw = resolve_week(games, config.TEAM, season, week=week)
    con = pff.connect()
